## 35. Stat Contributor Registry

Where: `game/simulation/entities/stat_contributors/`.

Contract:
- `STAT_CONTRIBUTOR_REGISTRY` is the single Phase-3 stat aggregation pipeline.
- `ShipStatsCalculator._phase_stats_aggregation` iterates `STAT_CONTRIBUTOR_REGISTRY.iter_for(comp)` once per operational component.
- Built-ins are registered entries seeded after domain modules load with explicit `phase_order`: movement=10, defense=20, hangar=40, command=50.
- Modder entries default to `phase_order=99`, after non-replaced built-ins.
- `StatAccumulator` is a typed `slots=True` dataclass with 10 scalar fields and 4 named map fields; misspelled scalar/map fields raise.
- Dynamic resource keys (`max_<resource>`, `gen_<resource>`) live inside `acc.resource_storage` / `acc.resource_generation`.
- Conflict policies: `REPLACE_WARN`, `REPLACE_SILENT`, `APPEND`, `ERROR`.
- `REPLACE_*` entries suppress the underlying default while active; unregistering restores the default.
- `register_stat_contributor(...)` returns a `RegistrationHandle`; unregister by handle.
- Defaults cannot be unregistered by handle; `reset_stat_contributor_registry()` clears and re-seeds.
- `CREW_PRIORITY_REGISTRY` is separate and maps ability names to crew allocation priority.
- This registry is distinct from `combat.ability_stat_registry.ABILITY_STAT_REGISTRY`; the latter emits battle modifier entries, this one aggregates component stats.
- Acceptance tests: `tests/unit/simulation/entities/stat_contributors/test_registry_pipeline.py` and `tests/unit/simulation/entities/test_stat_contributor_extension.py`.

To add a recalculation-time stat ability: define a contributor taking `(ship, comp, accumulator)`, register it for the ability name with an explicit conflict policy, capture the handle, and reset/unregister in tests.

Boundary:
- Phase-5 helpers such as `weapons.aggregate_targeting_scores`, `defense.apply_armor_and_repair_scores`, and `defense.init_armor_pool` remain imperative after the Phase-4 physics boundary. Folding them into the registry requires a future design.

## 36. Re-Export Shim

> **Last verified:** 2026-05-08 (PROJ-396 MAJ-006: Pattern #5 facade-bypass prohibition added)

Where (remaining confirmed sites; PROJ-416 deleted `race_setup_screen.py` and PROJ-417 deleted `test_run_details.py`, 2026-05-13):
- (Removed PROJ-417) `game/ui/screens/test_lab/test_run_details.py` â€”
  the ~12-LOC re-export shim is deleted; callers import
  `TestRunDetailsPanel` from `game/ui/screens/test_lab/details/` directly.
- `game/simulation/components/component.py:395-405` â€” re-exports
  loader symbols from `game/simulation/components/component_loader.py`.
- (Removed PROJ-416) `game/ui/screens/race_setup_screen.py` â€”
  the transitional re-export shim is deleted; all callers import
  from `game/ui/screens/race_setup/screen.py` directly.
- (Removed PROJ-383) `game/strategy/engine/command_handlers.py` â€”
  the transitional re-export shim is deleted; all callers import
  from `game/strategy/engine/handlers/base.py` directly.

Problem the pattern solves:
- A module is decomposed into a sub-package (or sibling module) but
  many existing imports still target the original path. Editing every
  importer in one PR enlarges the change footprint and complicates
  review/rollback. A thin re-export shim preserves the legacy import
  path while the canonical implementation moves.

Structure:
- The shim file is small (â‰¤ ~30 LOC) and contains only `from <new
  path> import <name>` lines plus an `__all__` listing of the
  re-exported names.
- A header docstring identifies the canonical module and the project
  / migration that introduced the shim.
- Tests that exercise behavior import from the canonical module.

When to use:
- Decomposing a god-module into a sub-package mid-refactor.
- Renaming a module while letting downstream call sites migrate
  incrementally (e.g. across multiple PROJs).
- Promoting an internal symbol to a new canonical home without a
  hard, repository-wide rename pass in a single change.

When NOT to use:
- For "compatibility" with old save files or external API consumers
  outside the repo â€” Rule 3 (Root Cause Fixes) prohibits compat shims
  for either. Re-export shims are an internal-migration aid only.
- To paper over genuinely unmigrated state. The shim is a temporary
  scaffold tied to a tracked decomposition project; it does not
  legitimize a permanent two-path import surface.
- When the canonical home is uncertain. Decide before introducing the
  shim; otherwise the shim becomes a permanent fixture.
- To create a public import surface that bypasses a Facade
  (Pattern #5). PROJ-382 Phase 1 specifically eradicated facade-bypass
  paths from `BuildQueueScreen` and `EmpireBuildQueueWindow`; a
  re-export shim that exposes internal delegate symbols the Facade
  is supposed to hide reopens the same hole under a new name.
  Facade-bypass sites must route through the Facade â€” never through a
  re-export shim, a renamed kwarg (e.g. `portrait_session=`), or any
  other indirection that re-exposes the underlying session/object.

Retirement:
- Each shim should reference the project responsible for migrating
  its callers (e.g. PROJ-302 for race_setup; PROJ-383 retired the
  former command_handlers shim).
- When the legacy import path has zero remaining call sites under
  `game/`, delete the shim file in the same PR that removes the last
  caller. Audit guard: a periodic grep for shim contents is the
  current detection mechanism; a future audit may add a static check.

## 37. Typed `DeployedGroup` Family (sibling of `Fleet`)

Where: `game/strategy/data/deployed_group.py` (`DeployedGroup`
abstract base + `MineGroup` / `FighterWing` /
`SatelliteConstellation`); `game/strategy/data/empire.py`
(`Empire.deployed_groups`, `add_deployed_group`,
`remove_deployed_group`, `deployed_groups_of`); the five FMS order
handlers under `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/`
(`lay_mines.py`, `launch_fighters.py`, `launch_satellites.py`,
`recover_fighters.py`, `recover_satellites.py`); combat seam at
`game/strategy/combat/spec_compiler.py` /
`game/strategy/combat/team_spec_builder.py`; minefield seam at
`game/strategy/engine/minefield_resolver.py`.

Replaces the retired (PROJ-431 / TD-10) "Group-Kind Fleet
Discriminator" pattern in which `Fleet.group_kind` âˆˆ
`{"fleet", "mine_group", "fighter_group", "satellite_group"}` plus
`BaseCommandHandler._reject_if_non_fleet_group` constrained
non-`fleet` Fleet kinds from movement / build / warp / intercept /
join commands. `Fleet.group_kind`, the guard, and the synthetic
mine-carrier `ShipInstance` are all DELETED.

Contract:
- Concrete subclasses register their `type` discriminator string via
  `@_register_type("<name>")` and implement `_from_dict_payload(data)`
  for polymorphic round-trip via `DeployedGroup.from_dict`.
- The base class deliberately exposes a NARROW surface: identity
  (`id`, `owner_id`, `location: HexCoord`, `display_name`) only.
  Fleet-action methods (Move / Warp / Build / Join) are NOT present.
  The runtime type IS the model; there is no string discriminator
  and no validation guard â€” deployed groups never reach fleet-action
  handlers because they are not `Fleet`s.
- `Empire.fleets` and `Empire.deployed_groups` are disjoint
  collections. Combat membership: the spec compiler walks both
  `empire.fleets` and `empire.deployed_groups_of(FighterWing |
  SatelliteConstellation)` for the at-hex participant set;
  `MineGroup`s are routed into the typed `mine_groups` sidecar on
  `StrategyBattleAssembly.extensions`.
- Strategic launch / lay actions mint a fresh group every time â€” no
  same-hex auto-merge for new launches (PROJ-FMS-B audit Fix 4;
  mirrored by PROJ-FMS-C / PROJ-FMS-D). End-of-battle fighter /
  satellite overflow DOES merge into a pre-existing same-type group
  at the sector when present.
- ID namespace conventions: `MineGroup` 100000+, `FighterWing`
  200000+, `SatelliteConstellation` 300000+.

`_ShipBearingDeployedGroup` is an internal (non-registered) base
for groups whose `ships` are real `ShipInstance` entries
(`FighterWing`, `SatelliteConstellation`). It supplies
`remove_ship` so the PROJ-269 post-battle hook prunes destroyed
ships via the same `IFleetMutator` plumbing used for real Fleets.

Use for: any new "empire-owned, hex-located deployable" entity that
conceptually is NOT a Fleet (no orders, no strategic move, no
shipyard). Add a new subclass under `deployed_group.py`, register
its `type`, and let the combat / DTO / serialisation paths pick it
up via `empire.deployed_groups_of(<NewType>)`.

Boundary: real fleets (have orders, can move, can build) remain
`Fleet`s on `empire.fleets`. Do not bolt a deployable concept onto
`Fleet` â€” extend the `DeployedGroup` family instead.

## 38. CarriedVehicle Substrate

Where: `game/strategy/data/ship_instance.py::ShipInstance.bay_inventory`
(typed `BayInventory.bay: list[CarriedVehicle]` slot â€” PROJ-436
Phase 9 deleted the legacy `_CarriedItemsProxy` shim and the
`carried_items` property);
`game/simulation/components/abilities/vehicle_bay.py::VehicleBayAbility`;
`game/strategy/data/carried_vehicle_deploy.py::carried_vehicle_to_ship_instance`;
`game/strategy/data/ship_cargo_manager.py`; order handlers under
`game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/` for launch / recovery.

Contract:
- `VehicleBayAbility` data shape: `{"capacity_mass": <int>,
  "allowed_types": ["mine", "fighter", "satellite"]}`. `allowed_types`
  is the typed-bay filter â€” `fighter_bay` carries `["fighter"]`,
  `satellite_bay` carries `["satellite"]`, `mine_bay` carries
  `["mine"]`, and universal `vehicle_bay` carries all three. Capacity
  scales via the `simple_size_mount` modifier and the
  `bay_capacity_mult` stat key (Round 4 Obs C).
- `CarriedVehicle` (a typed payload in `bay_inventory.bay`) holds
  `design_id`, `design_data`, `current_hp`, optional
  `component_states`, and `vehicle_type`. Mass is the capacity gate;
  `ShipCargoManager.can_accept_vehicle` queries `allowed_types`.
- Deploy: `carried_vehicle_to_ship_instance(cv, fleet_id, ...)` is the
  single shared helper that mints a deployed `ShipInstance` from a
  `CarriedVehicle`, preserving HP and per-component damage. Used by
  both strategic launch order handlers and tactical
  `BattleEngine.launch_*_in_battle`.
- Reboard: `fighter_reboard.apply_reboard` and the satellite reboard
  hook convert deployed `ShipInstance`s back into `CarriedVehicle`s
  appended to the recovering carrier's `bay_inventory.bay` (HP +
  component_states preserved).

Use for: any future design-backed cargo (drones, drop pods, boarding
craft). Reuse `VehicleBayAbility` with a new `vehicle_type` plus an
`allowed_types` entry on the bay rather than inventing a parallel
storage concept.

Boundary: drop pods and other non-design-backed cargo live in
`bay_inventory.pods` as typed `DropPod` entries. The
`bay_inventory.resources` / `bay_inventory.population` slots **exist**
(PROJ-436 Phase 2 widening) but production fleet-cargo today still
routes through the Phase 3 `ShipCargoManager` / `_cargo_contents`
substrate exposed via `Fleet.get_cargo_resource` /
`consume_cargo_resource`; migration into the typed BayInventory
slots is intentionally deferred (no production caller needs it
today). The four-slot `BayInventory` is the canonical
**typed** surface for `bay` and `pods`; `VehicleBay` capacity gates
only the `bay` slot's `CarriedVehicle` items.

## 39. Typed-Sidecar Extensions on Frozen DTOs

Where: `game/strategy/combat/battle_assembly.py::BattleSpecExtensions`,
`StrategyBattleAssembly`, `StrategyBattleAssembler`;
`game/simulation/battle_spec.py::BattleSpec` (frozen target).

Contract:
- A frozen simulation-layer DTO (e.g. `BattleSpec`) is a layer-spanning
  contract â€” strategy code MUST NOT mutate it. Strategy-only state that
  the simulation later needs is bundled in a typed `Extensions`
  dataclass wrapped alongside the spec by a typed
  `StrategyBattleAssembly`.
- Mutation requirements that must survive the frozen contract (e.g.
  a one-slot list filled by a pre-tick callback so a post-battle hook
  can read it) live as a mutable container field inside the otherwise
  frozen extensions dataclass. The frozen dataclass holds the reference;
  the container is appended to, never replaced.
- The orchestrator (`StrategyBattleAssembler.assemble`) is the only path
  that constructs both halves so spec and extensions cannot drift.
- Replaces the deprecated `object.__setattr__(frozen_dto, "_attr", value)`
  side-channel anti-pattern eliminated by PROJ-426 (TD-01).

Use for: any future cross-layer DTO where one side owns immutability
and the other needs to attach context, lifecycle state, or
extension-point data.

Boundary: fields that genuinely belong on the simulation contract
(read by `run_battle` / engine subsystems via their public surface)
go on the frozen DTO itself. Strategy-only data that the simulation
never reads goes on the extensions dataclass.

## 40. Named Pre-Tick Setup Registry

Where: `game/strategy/combat/pre_tick_setup_registry.py::PreTickBattleSetupRegistry`;
`game/strategy/combat/pre_tick_setup/{mine,reboard}_setup.py`;
`game/strategy/combat/battle_assembly.py::StrategyBattleAssembler`;
`game/simulation/battle_runner.py::run_battle`
(`pre_tick_loop_callback` parameter).

Contract:
- `run_battle` accepts a single `pre_tick_loop_callback(engine,
  battle_spec)` invoked once after engine construction and before the
  tick loop starts.
- Independent subsystems (mine resolvers, fighter reboard tracker,
  etc.) each export a `build_*_setup(...)` factory under
  `game/strategy/combat/pre_tick_setup/` that returns its own closure.
- `PreTickBattleSetupRegistry.register(name, setup)` adds a setup
  callback under a string name (duplicate names raise);
  `composed_callback()` returns a single ordered callback (registration
  order) or `None` when the registry is empty.
- `StrategyBattleAssembler` populates the registry once per assembly;
  the adapter passes `assembly.pre_tick_setup.composed_callback()`
  straight to `run_battle`.

Use for: any new battle-setup wiring that needs to install state on
the live `BattleEngine` before the tick loop. Register a named setup
with the assembler rather than racing for the single `pre_tick_loop_callback`
slot or adding a parallel kwarg to `run_battle`.

Boundary: things that need to run per-tick belong in the tick-phase
registry (Pattern #23). Things that need to run at end-of-battle
belong on the strategy post-battle hook
(`PostBattleHookBuilder.build`), not on this setup registry.

## 41. Polymorphic Order Issuer (`IIssuerAdapter`)

Where: `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py::IIssuerAdapter`,
`FleetShipIssuerAdapter`, `PlanetStagingYardIssuerAdapter`; the five
FMS order handlers under `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/`
(`lay_mines.py`, `launch_fighters.py`, `launch_satellites.py`,
`recover_fighters.py`, `recover_satellites.py`);
`game/strategy/engine/action_execution_engine.py`.

Contract:
- `IIssuerAdapter` is a `@runtime_checkable` Protocol exposing the
  minimum slice of fleet/planet that the FMS order handlers need:
  `location`, `owner_id`, `display_label`, `pop_carried(...)`,
  `count_carried(...)`, `append_carried(...)`, `append_recovered(...)`.
- Two production implementations: `FleetShipIssuerAdapter` wraps a
  `(Fleet, ShipInstance)` pair and operates on
  `ship.bay_inventory.bay` (typed `CarriedVehicle` entries â€” the
  Phase 9 deletion of the legacy `carried_items` shim made the typed
  slot the canonical write surface); `PlanetStagingYardIssuerAdapter`
  wraps a `Planet` and operates on `planet.staging_yard`
  (capacity-checked via `Planet.add_to_staging_yard`).
- Order handlers expose `execute_for_issuer(*, issuer, order_owner,
  empire, galaxy=None, registries=None) -> OrderExecutionResult` (the
  PROJ-438 Phase 6 unified 5-kwarg signature; recovery handlers accept
  and ignore the trailing `galaxy` / `registries`) and treat the
  `IIssuerAdapter` as the only mutation surface â€” no direct
  `fleet.ships[i].bay_inventory.bay` access.
- `ActionExecutionEngine` ticks both `fleet.orders` and `planet.orders`
  in Round 4; each iteration constructs the matching adapter and
  dispatches to the same handler.
- All five FMS `Issue*Command` DTOs carry an optional `planet_id`
  alongside the existing `fleet_id`; exactly one must be set.

Recipe (when adding a new issuer kind, e.g. orbital platform):

1. Define a new `IIssuerAdapter` implementation that exposes the
   minimum surface (location / owner_id / carried-vehicle pop+append).
2. Widen the `Issue*Command` DTOs in scope with an optional
   identifier for the new issuer kind.
3. Update the FMS command handlers' validation to recognise the new
   identifier and confirm the issuer holds the required capability
   ability.
4. Update `ActionExecutionEngine` to tick the new issuer's order list
   and construct the new adapter.
5. The five FMS order handlers should require no change â€” they
   already operate on `IIssuerAdapter`.

Use for: any new "thing that can issue strategic action orders"
(orbital platform, space station, megastructure, etc.) that should
reuse the existing FMS order pipeline rather than spawn a parallel
handler family.

Boundary: this pattern is for sharing handler logic across issuer
kinds. It is NOT for adding new order types â€” those still get their
own command + handler + order handler trio (Pattern #7).

## 42. Bootstrap-State Single Assignment Path

Where: `game/strategy/engine/session/runtime_services.py`, `game/strategy/engine/session/bootstrap.py`, `game/strategy/engine/session/persistence_adapter.py`, `game/strategy/engine/game_session.py`.

Use this pattern when a class has two construction entry paths (e.g. fresh construction + rehydration from a save) that must produce structurally identical instances. The historical failure mode is service-wiring drift: the two paths re-implement composition by hand, a new dependency lands on one path, and the other quietly diverges. PROJ-396 CRIT-002 is the canonical case in this codebase â€” the prior `GameSession` had a hand-mirrored mutator-service / turn-engine / event-bus block in both `__init__` and `from_dict`.

Contract:

- Define a single frozen-dataclass payload (e.g. `SessionBootstrapState`) that captures everything either path needs to apply onto `self`.
- Define a single internal assignment method (e.g. `_apply_bootstrap_state(state)`) that is the **only** place that mutates `self` from a state value. Do NOT use `self.__dict__.update(...)` or `cls.__new__(cls)` re-construction.
- Define a single canonical wiring function (e.g. `SessionBootstrap._build_services(...)`) shared by both paths.
- Both entry paths build a state and call the assignment method. Public API stays the same; tests should not see the indirection.
- Cover with an anti-drift regression test that compares service classes across both construction paths (e.g. `test_init_and_from_dict_use_identical_service_classes`).

Skeleton:

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SessionRuntimeServices:
    registries: GameRegistries
    event_log: EventLog
    # ... other wired services

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class SessionBootstrapState:
    config: GameConfig
    services: SessionRuntimeServices
    # ... other owned state

class SessionBootstrap:
    @staticmethod
    def _build_services(*, registries, event_log=None, ...): ...

    @staticmethod
    def new_game_state(config, *, ai_factory=None) -> SessionBootstrapState: ...

class GameSession:
    def __init__(self, config=None, ai_factory=None, *, _state=None):
        self._race_registry = None
        if _state is not None:
            self._apply_bootstrap_state(_state)
            return
        state = SessionBootstrap.new_game_state(config or GameConfig(), ai_factory=ai_factory)
        self._apply_bootstrap_state(state)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, data, ai_factory=None):
        session = cls.__new__(cls)
        session._race_registry = None
        state = SessionPersistenceAdapter.rehydrate_state(data, ai_factory=ai_factory, ...)
        session._apply_bootstrap_state(state)
        return session

    def _apply_bootstrap_state(self, state):
        # Single state-mutation site.
        self._services = state.services
        # ... other owned fields
```

Boundary: this pattern is for *structural* drift, not behavioral cleanup. If the two construction paths have intentionally different semantics (e.g. `human_player_ids` fallback differing between fresh and load paths), keep that asymmetry inside the state-builder for each path. The single-assignment method only copies from the state; it does not enforce equality across paths.

## 43. Unified Container Substrate

Where: `game/strategy/data/container.py::Container` (PROJ-436 Phase 0
substrate), `game/strategy/data/containable.py`,
`game/strategy/data/bay_inventory.py::BayInventory` (Phase 2 widened to
the four-slot Container projection), `game/strategy/engine/production_engine.py::IProductionResourceSource`
(Phase 8 polymorphic-protocol seam).

Use this pattern when a storage surface needs to hold heterogeneous
mass-priced content (resources, items, population) under one
capacity cap with one policy filter. PROJ-436 unified eight separate
storage fields and three ability variants (`ResourceStorage`,
`CargoStorage`, `VehicleBay`) into one `Container` abstraction; the
typed `BayInventory` shipped four parallel slots
(`bay: list[CarriedVehicle]`, `pods: list[DropPod]`,
`resources: dict[str, float]`, `population: dict[str, int]`) sharing
one mass cap.

Contract:

- `Container(capacity_mass, policy, resources, items, population)`
  carries three internal slices. Mass is the universal capacity gate
  â€” resource mass-per-unit resolves through
  `ResourceCatalog.get_mass_per_unit()`; item mass comes from the
  `ItemRef`; population mass comes from `species_mass_per_unit()`.
- `ContainerPolicy(allowed_kinds, allowed_type_ids=None)` filters by
  `ContainableKind` (RESOURCE / ITEM / POPULATION) plus an optional
  type-id allowlist. Policy is data, not code â€” a `metals_silo` with
  `allowed_type_ids=["metals"]` and a generic cargo hold with
  `allowed_type_ids=None` use the same engine path.
- `Container.accepts(containable)` is the policy seam for
  container-backed write paths and the unified projection surface
  (`BayInventory.container_view()` is a snapshot for callers that
  want unified accounting). **Transfer-kind validation does NOT go
  through `Container.accepts()` today** â€” `TransferValidator._is_known_cargo_type`
  routes through `ResourceCatalog.has()` plus three categorical
  sentinels (`passengers`, `drop_pod`, `vehicle`) directly; a future
  pass could wire the validator through `Container.accepts()` if a
  per-container policy check is needed, but that is not the current
  contract.
- For the production-engine read/consume path, the
  `IProductionResourceSource` Protocol (Phase 8) is the narrower
  polymorphic seam â€” `Planet` (over its stockpile API) and `Fleet`
  (over its cargo API) both satisfy
  `production_has_resources` / `production_get_resource` /
  `production_consume_resource`. The engine reads through these
  three methods without dispatching on entity type.
- Test-only: `set_resource_catalog(catalog)` on `container.py` injects
  a deterministic catalog for unit tests (PROJ-258
  `get_default_*` / `set_default_*` accessor convention).

Use for: any new storage surface that holds mixed mass-priced
content (drones-on-a-shipyard, planet-side civilian housing, etc.).
Reuse `Container` with a tailored `ContainerPolicy` rather than
inventing a parallel typed-list field per category. For
production-engine integration, satisfy `IProductionResourceSource`
via thin polymorphic delegators (do not extend the Protocol with
entity-specific methods).

Boundary: launch / recovery / life support / production stay
**separate** abilities â€” `Container` is storage only. Today's
**live** write substrates remain typed: `CarriedVehicle` items live
in `BayInventory.bay` (a `list[CarriedVehicle]` â€” see Pattern #38);
`DropPod` items live in `BayInventory.pods` (a `list[DropPod]`);
`Planet.stockpile` is a `dict[str, float]` over the `IStockpileHolder`
protocol; fleet cargo aggregates per-ship `_cargo_contents`
substrate through `Fleet.get_cargo_resource` /
`consume_cargo_resource` (the `BayInventory.resources` slot exists
from Phase 2 widening but production cargo has not been migrated
into it). `Container` and `Container.accepts()` are the unified
projection / policy seam over those typed substrates, not a
wholesale replacement of them â€” `BayInventory.container_view()`
returns a snapshot, not a mutable view. Deployed groups (`FighterWing`,
`SatelliteConstellation`, `MineGroup` on `empire.deployed_groups`)
are not in any container â€” Container handles only pre-deployment /
post-recovery storage. See Pattern #37 for the typed `DeployedGroup`
family.

> **Last verified:** 2026-05-18 â€” PROJ-436 Phase 10 doc refresh +
> Phase 11 consult disposition.
> Container substrate landed in Phase 0; `BayInventory` widened to
> four slots in Phase 2; `TransferValidator.VALID_CARGO_TYPES`
> deleted in Phase 7 â€” replaced by `ResourceCatalog.has()` + three
> categorical sentinels (`Container.accepts()` is the analogous
> seam for container-backed write paths but is NOT called by the
> current transfer validator);
> `ProductionEngine.context_type` storage-dispatch deleted in
> Phase 8 via the `IProductionResourceSource` Protocol;
> `_CarriedItemsProxy` deleted in Phase 9.

## Critical Naming Reminders

- Ship inherits `(PhysicsBody, ShipPhysicsMixin)` â€” there is no `ShipCombatMixin`.
- Config classes in `game/core/config.py` are plain classes, not dataclasses.
- Use `BattleScreen` / `StrategyScreen`, not `BattleScene` / `StrategyScene`.
- Use `VehicleDesignService`, not `ShipBuilderService`.
- `PolicyManager` lives at `game/ai/policy_manager.py`.
- Workshop `EventBus` lives at `game/ui/screens/builder/event_bus.py`; it is distinct from `game/core/event_logging.py::EventBus` used by simulation/strategy logging.
- Galaxy/Planet/Star read protocols (`IGalaxySystemGraph`, `IGalaxySpatialQuery`, `IHabitabilityCalculator`, `IStockpileHolder`, `IStagingYardHolder`) live at `game/strategy/data/galaxy_protocols.py`, beside the data classes; the cross-layer protocol package is `game/core/protocols/`.
- Mutator protocols (`IFleetMutator`, `IPlanetMutator`, `IEmpireMutator`, `IShipInstanceMutator`) live at `game/core/protocols/strategy_mutators.py`.

## Extension Checklist

- New battle launch: compile `BattleSpec`; call `run_battle` or `BattleController.start_from_spec`; pass `registry_provider` when no ship builder is supplied.
- New strategic effect source: implement `IAbilitySource`, register source provider, add owner/scope validation tests.
- New combat modifier ability: register in `ABILITY_STAT_REGISTRY`, update `KNOWN_EXTERNAL_STAT_KEYS`, add tests through quickstart complex coverage.

47:def _pod_from_dict(item: Any) -> DropPod:
48:    """Promote a drop-pod-shaped dict to a typed :class:`DropPod`.
49:
50:    Two shapes are supported:
51:
52:    * Save-shape (Phase 2+): ``{design_id, design_data, mass,
53:      payload: {...}}`` â€” matches :meth:`DropPod.to_dict`. The
54:      ``payload`` value is used as-is.
55:    * Legacy flat shape (pre-Phase-2 staging-yard substrate, fixtures,
56:      direct dict callers): any other keys (``name``, ``vehicle_type``,
57:      ``owner_id`` etc.) land in :attr:`DropPod.payload`.
58:    """
59:    if isinstance(item, DropPod):
60:        return item
61:    if not isinstance(item, dict):
62:        return DropPod(design_id="", design_data={}, mass=0.0, payload={})
63:    if "payload" in item and isinstance(item["payload"], dict):
64:        return DropPod.from_dict(item)
65:    return DropPod(
66:        design_id=str(item.get("design_id", "")),
67:        design_data=dict(item.get("design_data", {})),
68:        mass=float(item.get("mass", 0.0)),
69:        payload={
70:            k: v for k, v in item.items()
71:            if k not in {"design_id", "design_data", "mass"}
72:        },
73:    )

342:    # --- IStockpileHolder protocol (PROJ-372) ---
343:
344:    def add_to_stockpile(self, resource_type: str, amount: float) -> float:
345:        """Add resources to the local stockpile; return overflow."""
346:        current = self._stockpile.get(resource_type, 0.0)
347:        max_cap = self._max_stockpile.get(resource_type, float('inf'))
348:        new_total = current + amount
349:        if new_total > max_cap:
350:            self._stockpile[resource_type] = max_cap
351:            return new_total - max_cap
352:        self._stockpile[resource_type] = new_total
353:        return 0.0
354:
355:    def consume_from_stockpile(self, resource_type: str, amount: float) -> bool:
356:        """All-or-nothing consume. Return True iff sufficient stockpile."""
357:        current = self._stockpile.get(resource_type, 0.0)
358:        if current >= amount:
359:            self._stockpile[resource_type] = current - amount
360:            return True
361:        return False
362:
363:    def has_stockpile(self, costs: dict) -> bool:
364:        """True iff every resource->amount in `costs` is satisfied."""
365:        return all(
366:            self._stockpile.get(rt, 0.0) >= amt for rt, amt in costs.items()
367:        )

370:        """Current stockpiled amount, 0.0 if absent."""
371:        return self._stockpile.get(resource_type, 0.0)

175:                continue
176:            pod_mass = item.get("mass", 0.0)
177:            # Find a ship that can carry this pod
178:            target_ship = None
179:            for ship in fleet.ships:
180:                capacity = ship._cargo_mgr.get_pod_storage_capacity()
181:                used = ship._cargo_mgr.get_pod_storage_used()
182:                can = ship._cargo_mgr.can_carry_pod(pod_mass)
183:                logger.debug(
184:                    f"  Ship {ship.name}: pod_capacity={capacity} used={used} "
185:                    f"can_carry({pod_mass})={can}"
186:                )
187:                if can:
188:                    target_ship = ship
189:                    break
190:            if target_ship is None:
191:                logger.warning(
192:                    f"  No ship can carry pod '{item.get('name')}' (mass={pod_mass})"
193:                )
194:                continue  # No ship has capacity
195:            # PROJ-450 Phase 1: pop via the typed API; the dict â†” DropPod
196:            # promotion lives inside Planet. The peek+filter above already
197:            # rejected CarriedVehicle-shaped entries, so the typed return
198:            # is a DropPod here.

200:            if isinstance(typed, DropPod):

202:                current_bay = target_ship.bay_inventory
203:                new_pods = list(current_bay.pods)

206:                    BayInventory(bay=list(current_bay.bay), pods=new_pods)
207:                )
208:                loaded += 1
209:

278:    def _dispatch_carried_vehicle_load(
279:        self,
280:        fleet: Fleet,
281:        planet: "Planet",
282:        design_id: Optional[str] = None,
283:        amount: int = 0,
284:    ) -> int:
285:        """PROJ-FMS-A Phase 3: planet -> fleet, carried vehicle.
286:
287:        Generalised drop-pod load path for design-backed carried vehicles
288:        (mines / fighters / satellites). Loads from ``planet.staging_yard``
289:        into the first ship whose ``VehicleBay`` has compatible capacity.
290:        Staging yard iterated in reverse so ``pop`` removals are safe.
291:
292:        ``design_id`` may be passed via the legacy ``species_id`` slot in
293:        the order target dict â€” the order serializer treats the slot as
294:        a generic per-order discriminator.
295:
296:        PROJ-431 Phase 1d: staging-yard dict probe uses an explicit
297:        ``vehicle_type`` shape check instead of the legacy
298:        ``CarriedVehicle.from_any()`` discriminator. The staging yard
299:        is still on the dict substrate.
300:        """
301:        loaded = 0
302:        to_load = amount if amount > 0 else len(planet.staging_yard)
303:
304:        for i in range(len(planet.staging_yard) - 1, -1, -1):
305:            if loaded >= to_load:
306:                break
307:            item = planet.staging_yard[i]
308:            # Peek-filter before popping: skip drop-pod-shaped entries
309:            # and design_id mismatches without disturbing the substrate.
310:            if not _is_carried_vehicle_dict(item):
311:                continue
312:            peeked_design_id = (
313:                item.design_id if isinstance(item, CarriedVehicle)
314:                else str(item.get("design_id", ""))
315:            )
316:            if design_id and peeked_design_id != design_id:
317:                continue
318:            target_ship = None
319:            for ship in fleet.ships:
320:                # We need a typed CV for the capacity check; promote the
321:                # peeked dict without mutating the substrate.
322:                preview_cv = (
323:                    item if isinstance(item, CarriedVehicle)
324:                    else CarriedVehicle.from_dict(item)
325:                )
326:                if ship._cargo_mgr.can_accept_vehicle(preview_cv):
327:                    target_ship = ship
328:                    break
329:            if target_ship is None:
330:                continue
331:            # PROJ-450 Phase 1: pop via the typed API; the dict â†” typed
332:            # promotion lives inside Planet. The peek above guaranteed
333:            # CV shape, so the typed return is a CarriedVehicle here.
334:            typed = planet.pop_staging_yard_typed(i)
335:            if isinstance(typed, CarriedVehicle) and target_ship._cargo_mgr.load_vehicle(typed):
336:                loaded += 1
337:            elif typed is not None:
338:                # Restore: load failed unexpectedly. Route through the
339:                # capacity-checked API rather than the raw list to keep
340:                # the ``max_staging_mass`` invariant consistent with
341:                # every other staging-yard write site. The remove above
342:                # just freed this exact item's mass, so the cap allows
343:                # the rollback in normal operation; a False return here
344:                # would only happen if something else mutated the yard
345:                # concurrently, in which case dropping the item is
346:                # safer than violating the invariant.
347:                if not planet.add_to_staging_yard(typed):
348:                    logger.warning(
349:                        "_dispatch_carried_vehicle_load: rollback of %r dropped "
350:                        "(planet %s staging_yard capacity insufficient even though "
351:                        "the item was just removed â€” concurrent mutation suspected)",
352:                        typed, getattr(planet, "name", "?"),
353:                    )
354:        return loaded

359:        planet: "Planet",
360:        design_id: Optional[str] = None,
361:        amount: int = 0,
362:    ) -> int:
363:        """PROJ-FMS-A Phase 3: fleet -> planet, carried vehicle.
364:
365:        Mirror of :meth:`_dispatch_carried_vehicle_load`. Moves matching

369:        from game.strategy.data.carried_vehicle import CarriedVehicle
370:

373:        to_unload = amount if amount > 0 else total_count

388:                if planet.add_to_staging_yard(cv):
389:                    ship._cargo_mgr.unload_vehicle(idx)
390:                    unloaded += 1
391:        return unloaded

393:    def _dispatch_drop_pod_unload(
394:        self,
395:        fleet: Fleet,
396:        planet: "Planet",
397:        pod_name: Optional[str] = None,
398:        amount: int = 0,
399:    ) -> int:
400:        """Branch 6: fleet -> planet, drop_pod (unload to staging yard).
401:
402:        PROJ-431 Phase 1d: pods read from ``ship.bay_inventory.pods``
403:        (typed slot â€” exclusively drop pods by construction) and the
404:        consumed pod is removed by rebuilding the bay inventory and
405:        writing back via ``ship.set_bay_inventory(...)``.
406:
407:        PROJ-450 Phase 1: the typed ``DropPod`` is handed to
408:        ``planet.add_to_staging_yard`` directly; the dict-shape
409:        normalisation lives inside ``Planet`` now.
410:        """
411:        unloaded = 0
412:        # Count drop-pod entries via the typed slot; CarriedVehicle
413:        # entries belong to a different transfer branch.
414:        to_unload = amount if amount > 0 else sum(
415:            len(s.bay_inventory.pods) for s in fleet.ships
416:        )
417:
418:        for ship in fleet.ships:
419:            if unloaded >= to_unload:
420:                break

422:            # Walk a snapshot so we can rebuild the typed pod list
423:            # without index churn across mutations.
424:            kept_pods: List[DropPod] = []
425:            for pod in current_bay.pods:
426:                if unloaded >= to_unload:
427:                    kept_pods.append(pod)
428:                    continue
429:                if pod_name and pod.payload.get("name") != pod_name:
430:                    kept_pods.append(pod)
431:                    continue
432:                if planet.add_to_staging_yard(pod):
433:                    unloaded += 1
434:                    # pod consumed -- do not append to kept_pods
435:                else:
436:                    kept_pods.append(pod)
437:            if len(kept_pods) != len(current_bay.pods):
438:                ship.set_bay_inventory(
439:                    BayInventory(bay=list(current_bay.bay), pods=kept_pods)
440:                )
441:
442:        return unloaded

142:def test_planet_staging_yard_substrate_is_typed_not_dict() -> None:
143:    """``Planet._staging_yard`` MUST hold typed ``CarriedVehicle | DropPod``
144:    entries only; dict entries are forbidden.
145:
146:    PROJ-450 Phase 5 type-pin guard. The substrate was widened from
147:    ``List[Dict[str, Any]]`` to ``List[CarriedVehicle | DropPod]``.
148:    The ``add_to_staging_yard`` method normalises dict inputs to
149:    typed before appending, so any future regression that re-introduces
150:    a raw dict (via ``planet._staging_yard.append(legacy_dict)`` or
151:    similar back-door) is caught here.
152:
153:    The public ``Planet.staging_yard`` property returns
154:    ``tuple[CarriedVehicle | DropPod, ...]``; this guard pins the
155:    underlying storage shape.

3:Executes ``OrderType.LAY_MINES`` orders.
4:
5:QA Observation B refactor: the action is polymorphic across two issuer
6:kinds via :class:`IIssuerAdapter`:
7:
8:  * Fleet-issued: the order's ``ship_instance_id`` selects a carrier
9:    ship in the issuing fleet; the adapter wraps that ``(fleet, ship)``
10:    pair and the mines come from the carrier's typed
11:    :class:`BayInventory` bay slot.
12:  * Planet-issued: the engine builds a
13:    :class:`PlanetStagingYardIssuerAdapter` and the mines come from
14:    ``planet.staging_yard`` (still the legacy dict list).
15:
16:PROJ-431 Phase 2: mines now deposit into a typed :class:`MineGroup`
17:attached to ``empire.deployed_groups``. The synthetic mine-carrier
18:``ShipInstance`` (``mine_carrier_synthetic``) is deleted; the fake
19:zero-HP ship is no longer constructed. ``empire.fleets`` carries only
20:real fleets; the assembler and minefield resolver read mines off the
21:``deployed_groups`` collection.
22:
23:Order ``target`` payload is a dict::
24:
25:    {
26:        'ship_instance_id': str,    # Carrier ship (fleet-issued path); None
27:                                    # / absent for planet-issued.
28:        'mine_design_id': str,      # Specific design to lay
29:        'count': int,               # How many to lay
30:        'target_hex': HexCoord,     # Where to lay (default = issuer.location)

150:        empires: Optional[List["Empire"]] = None,
151:    ) -> OrderExecutionResult:
152:        order = fleet.get_current_order()
153:        if not order or order.type != OrderType.LAY_MINES:
154:            return OrderExecutionResult(success=False, message="Not a LAY_MINES order")

156:        payload = order.target

169:            )

184:    def execute_for_issuer(
185:        self,
186:        *,
187:        issuer: IIssuerAdapter,
188:        order_owner: Any,
189:        empire: "Empire",
190:        galaxy: "Galaxy",
191:        registries: Any = None,
192:    ) -> OrderExecutionResult:
193:        """Run the handler against any IIssuerAdapter (planet or fleet).
194:
195:        ``order_owner`` is the entity whose ``orders`` queue holds the
196:        active order â€” usually the same as the wrapped fleet/planet.
197:
198:        PROJ-445 Phase 1 (F-B-001): ``registries`` accepted to match the
199:        unified ``IOrderHandler`` 5-kwarg contract â€” see
200:        :meth:`game.strategy.engine.order_handlers.recover_fighters.RecoverFightersOrderHandler.execute_for_issuer`
201:        for the canonical accept-and-ignore shape. Without it,
202:        :meth:`ActionExecutionEngine._execute_planet_action` raises
203:        ``TypeError`` on any planet-issued ``LAY_MINES`` order.
204:        """
205:        del registries
206:        order = order_owner.get_current_order()
207:        if not order or order.type != OrderType.LAY_MINES:
208:            return OrderExecutionResult(success=False, message="Not a LAY_MINES order")
209:        payload = order.target
210:        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
211:            order_owner.pop_order()
212:            return OrderExecutionResult(
213:                success=False, message="LAY_MINES order missing payload"
214:            )
215:        return self._run_with_issuer(
216:            issuer=issuer,
217:            order_owner=order_owner,
218:            empire=empire,
219:            galaxy=galaxy,
220:            payload=payload,
221:        )

223:    def _run_with_issuer(
224:        self,
225:        *,
226:        issuer: IIssuerAdapter,
227:        order_owner: Any,
228:        empire: "Empire",
229:        galaxy: "Galaxy",
230:        payload: Dict[str, Any],
231:    ) -> OrderExecutionResult:
232:        mine_design_id = payload.get("mine_design_id")
233:        count_raw = payload.get("count", 0)
234:        try:
235:            count = int(count_raw) if count_raw is not None else 0
236:        except (TypeError, ValueError):
237:            count = 0
238:        target_hex = payload.get("target_hex") or issuer.location
239:
240:        if count <= 0:
241:            order_owner.pop_order()
242:            return OrderExecutionResult(
243:                success=False,
244:                message="LAY_MINES order requires count > 0",
245:            )
246:        # Normalise: an empty / falsy / "auto" design_id means "any mine"
247:        # so the handler's pop loop accepts any mine vehicle type.
248:        effective_design = mine_design_id if (mine_design_id and mine_design_id != "auto") else None
249:
250:        # Try to pop exactly `count` matching mines.
251:        popped = issuer.pop_carried("mine", effective_design, count)
252:        if len(popped) < count:
253:            # Put back; fail cleanly with no partial consumption.
254:            issuer.append_carried(popped)
255:            order_owner.pop_order()
256:            available = issuer.count_carried("mine", effective_design)
257:            return OrderExecutionResult(
258:                success=False,
259:                message=(
260:                    f"Insufficient mines: requested {count} of design "
261:                    f"{mine_design_id!r}, available {available}"
262:                ),
263:            )
264:
265:        # PROJ-431 Phase 2: deposit into a fresh ``MineGroup``. Each
266:        # IssueLayMinesCommand produces its own group â€” same-hex lays
267:        # do NOT auto-merge (PROJ-FMS-B audit Fix 4).
268:        mine_group = self._create_mine_group(
269:            empire=empire,
270:            target_hex=target_hex,
271:        )
272:        for mine in popped:
273:            if isinstance(mine, CarriedVehicle):
274:                mine_group.mines.append(mine)
275:            elif isinstance(mine, dict):
276:                mine_group.mines.append(CarriedVehicle.from_dict(mine))
277:
278:        mine_group.scatter_seed = _stable_scatter_seed(
279:            seed_namespace=self._balance.scatter.seed_namespace,
280:            owner_id=empire.id,
281:            hex_coord=target_hex,
282:            launch_turn=self._extract_turn(galaxy),
283:        )
284:        mine_group.mine_positions = _scatter_positions(
285:            count=len(mine_group.mines),
286:            seed=mine_group.scatter_seed,

288:        )

26:def check_issuer_invariant(cmd, action: str) -> Optional[ValidationResult]:
27:    """Validate exactly-one-of(fleet_id, planet_id) on FMS command DTOs.
28:
29:    Returns ``None`` when the invariant holds; otherwise an error result.
30:    """
31:    has_fleet = getattr(cmd, "fleet_id", None) is not None
32:    has_planet = getattr(cmd, "planet_id", None) is not None
33:    if has_fleet and has_planet:
34:        return ValidationResult.error(
35:            f"{action}: exactly one of fleet_id / planet_id allowed."
36:        )
37:    if not has_fleet and not has_planet:
38:        return ValidationResult.error(
39:            f"{action}: one of fleet_id / planet_id required."
40:        )
41:    return None

44:def count_matching_bay(
45:    bay: List[CarriedVehicle], vehicle_type: str, design_id
46:) -> int:
47:    """Count typed bay entries matching ``vehicle_type``/``design_id``.
48:
49:    PROJ-431 Phase 1c: typed counterpart to :func:`count_matching_yard`.
50:    Bays are homogeneous ``list[CarriedVehicle]`` so no
51:    ``from_any``-style discrimination is needed.
52:    """
53:    n = 0
54:    wants_any = (not design_id) or design_id == "auto"
55:    for cv in bay:
56:        if cv.vehicle_type != vehicle_type:
57:            continue
58:        if not wants_any and cv.design_id != design_id:
59:            continue
60:        n += 1
61:    return n

64:def count_matching_yard(
65:    items: Iterable, vehicle_type: str, design_id
66:) -> int:
67:    """Count ``CarriedVehicle``-shaped dict entries in a planet staging
68:    yard matching the filter.
69:
70:    PROJ-431 Phase 1f: the staging-yard substrate is still a mixed list
71:    of dicts (migration deferred to PROJ-425 Phase 6). Discrimination is
72:    an explicit isinstance + dict-shape probe; the legacy
73:    ``CarriedVehicle.from_any`` runtime discriminator has been deleted.
74:    """
75:    n = 0
76:    wants_any = (not design_id) or design_id == "auto"
77:    for item in items:
78:        if isinstance(item, CarriedVehicle):
79:            cv = item
80:        elif isinstance(item, dict) and str(
81:            item.get("vehicle_type", "")
82:        ).lower() in VALID_VEHICLE_TYPES:
83:            cv = CarriedVehicle.from_dict(item)
84:        else:
85:            continue
86:        if cv.vehicle_type != vehicle_type:
87:            continue
88:        if not wants_any and cv.design_id != design_id:
89:            continue
90:        n += 1
91:    return n

94:def resolve_requested(
95:    count: Optional[int], count_available: int
96:) -> int | ValidationResult:
97:    """Resolve the requested count.
98:
99:    Returns either an ``int`` (resolved count) or a ``ValidationResult``
100:    when the caller supplied a non-positive count.
101:    """
102:    if count is None:
103:        return count_available
104:    if count <= 0:
105:        return ValidationResult.error("Count must be > 0.")
106:    return int(count)

1:"""Polymorphic issuer adapter for FMS order handlers (QA Observation B).
2:
3:Background â€” both fleets AND planets can now issue strategic FMS orders
4:(``LAY_MINES``, ``LAUNCH_FIGHTERS``, ``LAUNCH_SATELLITES``,
5:``RECOVER_FIGHTERS``, ``RECOVER_SATELLITES``). Previously every order
6:handler reached directly into ``fleet.ships[i].carried_items``; widening
7:that contract one handler at a time would duplicate the new
8:planet-staging-yard branch in five places.
9:
10:This module introduces :class:`IIssuerAdapter` and two concrete
11:implementations:
12:
13:- :class:`FleetShipIssuerAdapter` wraps the existing
14:  ``(Fleet, ShipInstance)`` shape so order handlers can keep operating
15:  through one accessor surface. PROJ-431 Phase 1b routes all reads &
16:  writes through :attr:`ShipInstance.bay_inventory` /
17:  :meth:`ShipInstance.set_bay_inventory` instead of the legacy
18:  ``carried_items`` mixed list.
19:- :class:`PlanetStagingYardIssuerAdapter` wraps a :class:`Planet`'s
20:  ``staging_yard`` so the same handlers can serve planet-issued FMS
21:  actions without a parallel handler family. The staging yard is
22:  out-of-scope for PROJ-431 Phase 1b and remains a dict list for now.
23:
24:The adapter intentionally exposes the *minimum* set of fields the five
25:handlers touch today. New ops must extend this surface explicitly so the
26:contract stays small.

187:        return int(self._fleet.owner_id)
188:
189:    @property
190:    def display_label(self) -> str:
191:        name = getattr(self._fleet, "display_name", None)
192:        if name:
193:            return str(name)
194:        return f"Fleet {self._fleet.id}"
195:
196:    def pop_carried(
197:        self,
198:        vehicle_type: str,
199:        design_id: Optional[str],
200:        count: Optional[int],
201:    ) -> List[Any]:
202:        # PROJ-431 Phase 1c: return typed ``CarriedVehicle`` instances
203:        # straight from the typed BayInventory.bay slot. The dict-round-
204:        # trip from Phase 1b is gone â€” FMS order handlers now consume
205:        # the typed payload directly. Planet adapter's matching method
206:        # still yields dicts for the staging-yard substrate (out of
207:        # scope until 1d).
208:        current = self._ship.bay_inventory
209:        popped: List[CarriedVehicle] = []
210:        remaining_bay: List[CarriedVehicle] = []
211:        limit = count if (count is not None and count >= 0) else None
212:        for cv in current.bay:
213:            if limit is not None and len(popped) >= limit:
214:                remaining_bay.append(cv)
215:                continue
216:            if _cv_matches(cv, vehicle_type, design_id):
217:                popped.append(cv)
218:            else:
219:                remaining_bay.append(cv)
220:        self._ship.set_bay_inventory(
221:            BayInventory(bay=remaining_bay, pods=list(current.pods))
222:        )
223:        return popped
224:
225:    def count_carried(
226:        self,
227:        vehicle_type: str,
228:        design_id: Optional[str],
229:    ) -> int:
230:        return sum(
231:            1 for cv in self._ship.bay_inventory.bay
232:            if _cv_matches(cv, vehicle_type, design_id)
233:        )
234:
235:    def append_carried(self, items: List[Any]) -> int:
236:        # PROJ-431 Phase 1b: route writes through the typed BayInventory.
237:        # Items arrive from out-of-scope handlers as dicts (vehicle dicts
238:        # or pod dicts) or as already-typed CarriedVehicle instances;
239:        # accept both and route each into the correct typed slot.
240:        current = self._ship.bay_inventory
241:        new_bay = list(current.bay)
242:        new_pods = list(current.pods)
243:        appended = 0
244:        for item in items:
245:            if isinstance(item, CarriedVehicle):
246:                new_bay.append(item)
247:                appended += 1
248:                continue
249:            if isinstance(item, DropPod):
250:                new_pods.append(item)
251:                appended += 1
252:                continue
253:            if isinstance(item, dict):
254:                # PROJ-431 Phase 1f: explicit dict-shape probe replaces
255:                # the legacy ``CarriedVehicle.from_any`` discriminator.
256:                vt = str(item.get("vehicle_type", "")).lower()
257:                if vt in VALID_VEHICLE_TYPES:
258:                    new_bay.append(CarriedVehicle.from_dict(item))
259:                    appended += 1
260:                    continue
261:                # Drop-pod-shaped dict (or other non-vehicle payload) â€”
262:                # preserve in the pods slot.
263:                new_pods.append(DropPod.from_dict(item))
264:                appended += 1
265:        self._ship.set_bay_inventory(BayInventory(bay=new_bay, pods=new_pods))
266:        return appended
267:
268:    def append_recovered(self, vehicle: CarriedVehicle) -> bool:
269:        cargo_mgr = getattr(self._ship, "_cargo_mgr", None)
270:        if cargo_mgr is None:
271:            return False
272:        return bool(cargo_mgr.load_vehicle(vehicle))

176:def test_same_hex_lays_do_not_auto_merge(setup_empire_and_fleet):
177:    """PROJ-FMS-B audit Fix 4: same-hex lays by the same owner must NOT
178:    auto-merge into a single mine_group. The shared design says
179:    "Multiple groups per owner per hex permitted; no auto-merge"; the
180:    Phase 1 checklist agrees. Pre-fix the order handler returned the
181:    first matching mine_group at the hex, silently coalescing.
182:    """
183:    empire, fleet, carrier, galaxy = setup_empire_and_fleet
184:    handler = LayMinesOrderHandler()
185:
186:    # Lay 2 mines in the first action.
187:    fleet.add_order(Order(OrderType.LAY_MINES, target={
188:        "ship_instance_id": carrier.instance_id,
189:        "mine_design_id": "mine_warhead_small",
190:        "count": 2,
191:        "target_hex": fleet.location,
192:    }))
193:    handler.execute_action_order(fleet, empire, galaxy)
194:
195:    # Then lay 2 more in the same hex.
196:    fleet.add_order(Order(OrderType.LAY_MINES, target={
197:        "ship_instance_id": carrier.instance_id,
198:        "mine_design_id": "mine_warhead_small",
199:        "count": 2,
200:        "target_hex": fleet.location,
201:    }))
202:    handler.execute_action_order(fleet, empire, galaxy)
203:
204:    mine_groups = empire.deployed_groups
205:    # Two separate lay actions => two distinct mine_groups (no auto-merge).
206:    assert len(mine_groups) == 2
207:    counts = sorted(len(mg.mines) for mg in mine_groups)
208:    assert counts == [2, 2]

+
+## Findings
+
+- 1. F-B-013 is mostly closed at the data boundary. `Planet` now owns the three staging-yard helpers in `game/strategy/data/planet.py:33-87`, the substrate is annotated as `List[CarriedVehicle | DropPod]` in `game/strategy/data/planet.py:162-165`, `__post_init__` normalises raw entries in `game/strategy/data/planet.py:199-216`, `staging_yard` is a typed read-only tuple in `game/strategy/data/planet.py:330-340`, and public writes/pops normalise through `game/strategy/data/planet.py:404-454`. Save/load matches that contract: `_normalize_to_typed()` in `game/strategy/data/planet_serde.py:28-53` and `planet_from_dict_kwargs()` in `game/strategy/data/planet_serde.py:196` promote dict saves back to typed entries, while `planet_to_dict()` in `game/strategy/data/planet_serde.py:82-89` emits per-entry `.to_dict()` at the save boundary. `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:33-37` only imports `_is_carried_vehicle_dict`; the helpers are no longer defined there.
+- 2. DI-2026-05-18-001 substrate half is closed in the transfer path. The old flatten/inflate sites are gone from the planet load/unload branches: `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:195-207` pop via `planet.pop_staging_yard_typed()`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:331-348` use typed rollback via `planet.add_to_staging_yard(typed)`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:385-388` unload typed `CarriedVehicle` directly, and `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:407-432` unload typed `DropPod` directly. The planet issuer adapter likewise appends recovered typed vehicles straight through `planet.add_to_staging_yard(vehicle)` at `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py:362-365`.
+- 3. Blocker: `TransferValidator` still rejects real planet staging yards for `drop_pod` loads. In `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:226-231`, `_validate_load()` accepts only `list` and resets any non-list `staging_yard` to `[]`. Real `Planet.staging_yard` is now a `tuple` per `game/strategy/data/planet.py:330-340`, so planet to fleet drop-pod loads validate as empty even when pods are present. I verified this with a read-only runtime probe: a real `Planet` with one staged pod printed `tuple` for `type(planet.staging_yard).__name__` and then returned `False / "P has no items in staging yard."` from `TransferValidator._validate_load(...)`. By contrast, the typed vehicle path is correct: `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:340-393` iterates the tuple and accepts typed `CarriedVehicle`, and a runtime probe returned `True`.
+- 4. The Phase 3 reader / validator / write-service closures are otherwise in place. The UI reader no longer has the list-only silent-skip bug: `game/ui/screens/strategy_detail_fmt.py:284-316` handles `list | tuple` and typed `CarriedVehicle` / `DropPod` with dict fallback. The DTO and facade snapshot paths do the same at `game/strategy/facade/dto/planet_dto.py:115-146` and `game/strategy/facade/slices/planet_slice.py:194-226`. Integration tests stage typed inputs in `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_lay_mines.py:154-188` and `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_launch.py:152-228`. The validator/write-service surface is tightened at `game/core/protocols/strategy_mutators.py:106-114` and `game/strategy/services/planet_write_service.py:102-119`.
+- 5. The read-only property contract holds. Production `Planet` has no `@staging_yard.setter`; the getter-only property is at `game/strategy/data/planet.py:330-340`, and the static guard in `tests/static_guards/test_no_planet_legacy_kwarg_wrapper.py:88-99` enforces that. Repo search found `@staging_yard.setter` only in the test stub `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_launch.py:85-87`. A runtime probe against a real `Planet` raised `AttributeError: property 'staging_yard' of 'Planet' object has no setter` on `planet.staging_yard = ()`.
+- 6. Save-format compatibility is good for both shapes. New-shape saves are still dict-shaped at the boundary via `game/strategy/data/planet_serde.py:82-89`, and the regenerated fixture uses nested `payload` at `tests/fixtures/saves/galaxy_proj372_populated.json:1170-1178`. Old-shape flat pod dicts are still accepted by `_pod_from_dict()` at `game/strategy/data/planet.py:47-73`. I verified both read-only: a synthetic old-shape `Planet.from_dict(...)` produced a typed `DropPod` with payload `{'name': 'Legacy Pod', 'vehicle_type': 'drop_pod', 'owner_id': 7}`, and the regenerated fixture planet loaded to a typed `DropPod` with payload `{'ready_at_turn': 5}`.
+- 7. Residue remains, but most of it is non-blocking. `PlanetStagingYardIssuerAdapter.pop_carried()` still writes `self._planet._staging_yard = remaining` directly at `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py:323-336`; with a real `Planet` this preserves typed entries, so I do not see this as a blocker, but it still bypasses the Planet helper boundary. I also found stale comments that still describe the planet substrate as dict-based at `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py:19-23`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/lay_mines.py:12-15`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/launch_fighters.py:189-198`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/launch_satellites.py:172-181`, `game/strategy/engine/handlers/fms_shared.py:10-13`, and `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:352-356`.
+- 8. I found no production staging-yard writers under `game/` that still construct dict literals or call `add_to_staging_yard(cv.to_dict())`; repo search returned no matches for those patterns. The remaining dict-style staging-yard writes are in tests and save serialization only.
+- 9. The LOC ceiling was not reclaimed. The guard still says `PLANET_LOC_CEILING = 525` at `tests/unit/strategy/data/test_galaxy_planet_star_loc_ceilings.py:41-47`, but the current file length of `game/strategy/data/planet.py` is 436 LOC from a read-only line-count probe. So there is clear headroom to lower the ceiling; `510` would be safe immediately, and an even tighter ceiling is defensible if you want the guard to track the current file more closely.
+
+## Risks
+
+- The verified blocker is easy to miss because the relevant tests still use list-backed mocks instead of a real tuple-backed `Planet`: `tests/unit/strategy/validation/test_transfer_drop_pod.py:11-24`, `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_pod_transfer.py:59-78`, and `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_order_processor_transfer.py:224-243` / `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_order_processor_transfer.py:458-467` all stage pods or vehicles on mutable list mocks. That gap is why the tuple regression survived.
+- Several integration stubs still model `staging_yard` as dict-backed and/or writable, notably `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_launch.py:74-87` and `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_recovery.py:54-74` / `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_recovery.py:127-161`. They are not production blockers, but they continue to hide typed-substrate regressions and stale assumptions.
+- The stale comments around the issuer adapter and FMS handlers are not behavior bugs today, but they create bad follow-on guidance for future edits because they describe a substrate that no longer exists in production.
+
+## Open questions
+
+None.

+complete: true

+---
+
+## Findings
+
+- 1. F-B-013 is mostly closed at the data boundary. `Planet` now owns the three staging-yard helpers in `game/strategy/data/planet.py:33-87`, the substrate is annotated as `List[CarriedVehicle | DropPod]` in `game/strategy/data/planet.py:162-165`, `__post_init__` normalises raw entries in `game/strategy/data/planet.py:199-216`, `staging_yard` is a typed read-only tuple in `game/strategy/data/planet.py:330-340`, and public writes/pops normalise through `game/strategy/data/planet.py:404-454`. Save/load matches that contract: `_normalize_to_typed()` in `game/strategy/data/planet_serde.py:28-53` and `planet_from_dict_kwargs()` in `game/strategy/data/planet_serde.py:196` promote dict saves back to typed entries, while `planet_to_dict()` in `game/strategy/data/planet_serde.py:82-89` emits per-entry `.to_dict()` at the save boundary. `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:33-37` only imports `_is_carried_vehicle_dict`; the helpers are no longer defined there.
+- 2. DI-2026-05-18-001 substrate half is closed in the transfer path. The old flatten/inflate sites are gone from the planet load/unload branches: `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:195-207` pop via `planet.pop_staging_yard_typed()`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:331-348` use typed rollback via `planet.add_to_staging_yard(typed)`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:385-388` unload typed `CarriedVehicle` directly, and `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:407-432` unload typed `DropPod` directly. The planet issuer adapter likewise appends recovered typed vehicles straight through `planet.add_to_staging_yard(vehicle)` at `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py:362-365`.
+- 3. Blocker: `TransferValidator` still rejects real planet staging yards for `drop_pod` loads. In `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:226-231`, `_validate_load()` accepts only `list` and resets any non-list `staging_yard` to `[]`. Real `Planet.staging_yard` is now a `tuple` per `game/strategy/data/planet.py:330-340`, so planet to fleet drop-pod loads validate as empty even when pods are present. I verified this with a read-only runtime probe: a real `Planet` with one staged pod printed `tuple` for `type(planet.staging_yard).__name__` and then returned `False / "P has no items in staging yard."` from `TransferValidator._validate_load(...)`. By contrast, the typed vehicle path is correct: `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:340-393` iterates the tuple and accepts typed `CarriedVehicle`, and a runtime probe returned `True`.
+- 4. The Phase 3 reader / validator / write-service closures are otherwise in place. The UI reader no longer has the list-only silent-skip bug: `game/ui/screens/strategy_detail_fmt.py:284-316` handles `list | tuple` and typed `CarriedVehicle` / `DropPod` with dict fallback. The DTO and facade snapshot paths do the same at `game/strategy/facade/dto/planet_dto.py:115-146` and `game/strategy/facade/slices/planet_slice.py:194-226`. Integration tests stage typed inputs in `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_lay_mines.py:154-188` and `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_launch.py:152-228`. The validator/write-service surface is tightened at `game/core/protocols/strategy_mutators.py:106-114` and `game/strategy/services/planet_write_service.py:102-119`.
+- 5. The read-only property contract holds. Production `Planet` has no `@staging_yard.setter`; the getter-only property is at `game/strategy/data/planet.py:330-340`, and the static guard in `tests/static_guards/test_no_planet_legacy_kwarg_wrapper.py:88-99` enforces that. Repo search found `@staging_yard.setter` only in the test stub `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_launch.py:85-87`. A runtime probe against a real `Planet` raised `AttributeError: property 'staging_yard' of 'Planet' object has no setter` on `planet.staging_yard = ()`.
+- 6. Save-format compatibility is good for both shapes. New-shape saves are still dict-shaped at the boundary via `game/strategy/data/planet_serde.py:82-89`, and the regenerated fixture uses nested `payload` at `tests/fixtures/saves/galaxy_proj372_populated.json:1170-1178`. Old-shape flat pod dicts are still accepted by `_pod_from_dict()` at `game/strategy/data/planet.py:47-73`. I verified both read-only: a synthetic old-shape `Planet.from_dict(...)` produced a typed `DropPod` with payload `{'name': 'Legacy Pod', 'vehicle_type': 'drop_pod', 'owner_id': 7}`, and the regenerated fixture planet loaded to a typed `DropPod` with payload `{'ready_at_turn': 5}`.
+- 7. Residue remains, but most of it is non-blocking. `PlanetStagingYardIssuerAdapter.pop_carried()` still writes `self._planet._staging_yard = remaining` directly at `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py:323-336`; with a real `Planet` this preserves typed entries, so I do not see this as a blocker, but it still bypasses the Planet helper boundary. I also found stale comments that still describe the planet substrate as dict-based at `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py:19-23`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/lay_mines.py:12-15`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/launch_fighters.py:189-198`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/launch_satellites.py:172-181`, `game/strategy/engine/handlers/fms_shared.py:10-13`, and `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:352-356`.
+- 8. I found no production staging-yard writers under `game/` that still construct dict literals or call `add_to_staging_yard(cv.to_dict())`; repo search returned no matches for those patterns. The remaining dict-style staging-yard writes are in tests and save serialization only.
+- 9. The LOC ceiling was not reclaimed. The guard still says `PLANET_LOC_CEILING = 525` at `tests/unit/strategy/data/test_galaxy_planet_star_loc_ceilings.py:41-47`, but the current file length of `game/strategy/data/planet.py` is 436 LOC from a read-only line-count probe. So there is clear headroom to lower the ceiling; `510` would be safe immediately, and an even tighter ceiling is defensible if you want the guard to track the current file more closely.
+
+## Risks
+
+- The verified blocker is easy to miss because the relevant tests still use list-backed mocks instead of a real tuple-backed `Planet`: `tests/unit/strategy/validation/test_transfer_drop_pod.py:11-24`, `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_pod_transfer.py:59-78`, and `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_order_processor_transfer.py:224-243` / `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_order_processor_transfer.py:458-467` all stage pods or vehicles on mutable list mocks. That gap is why the tuple regression survived.
+- Several integration stubs still model `staging_yard` as dict-backed and/or writable, notably `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_launch.py:74-87` and `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_recovery.py:54-74` / `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_recovery.py:127-161`. They are not production blockers, but they continue to hide typed-substrate regressions and stale assumptions.
+- The stale comments around the issuer adapter and FMS handlers are not behavior bugs today, but they create bad follow-on guidance for future edits because they describe a substrate that no longer exists in production.
+
+## Open questions
+
+None.

I verified both read-only: a synthetic old-shape `Planet.from_dict(...)` produced a typed `DropPod` with payload `{'name': 'Legacy Pod', 'vehicle_type': 'drop_pod', 'owner_id': 7}`, and the regenerated fixture planet loaded to a typed `DropPod` with payload `{'ready_at_turn': 5}`.
- 7. Residue remains, but most of it is non-blocking. `PlanetStagingYardIssuerAdapter.pop_carried()` still writes `self._planet._staging_yard = remaining` directly at `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py:323-336`; with a real `Planet` this preserves typed entries, so I do not see this as a blocker, but it still bypasses the Planet helper boundary. I also found stale comments that still describe the planet substrate as dict-based at `game/strategy/engine/issuer_adapter.py:19-23`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/lay_mines.py:12-15`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/launch_fighters.py:189-198`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/launch_satellites.py:172-181`, `game/strategy/engine/handlers/fms_shared.py:10-13`, and `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:352-356`.
- 8. I found no production staging-yard writers under `game/` that still construct dict literals or call `add_to_staging_yard(cv.to_dict())`; repo search returned no matches for those patterns. The remaining dict-style staging-yard writes are in tests and save serialization only.
- 9. The LOC ceiling was not reclaimed. The guard still says `PLANET_LOC_CEILING = 525` at `tests/unit/strategy/data/test_galaxy_planet_star_loc_ceilings.py:41-47`, but the current file length of `game/strategy/data/planet.py` is 436 LOC from a read-only line-count probe. So there is clear headroom to lower the ceiling; `510` would be safe immediately, and an even tighter ceiling is defensible if you want the guard to track the current file more closely.

## Risks

- The verified blocker is easy to miss because the relevant tests still use list-backed mocks instead of a real tuple-backed `Planet`: `tests/unit/strategy/validation/test_transfer_drop_pod.py:11-24`, `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_pod_transfer.py:59-78`, and `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_order_processor_transfer.py:224-243` / `tests/unit/strategy/engine/test_order_processor_transfer.py:458-467` all stage pods or vehicles on mutable list mocks. That gap is why the tuple regression survived.
- Several integration stubs still model `staging_yard` as dict-backed and/or writable, notably `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_launch.py:74-87` and `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_recovery.py:54-74` / `tests/integration/test_fms_planet_recovery.py:127-161`. They are not production blockers, but they continue to hide typed-substrate regressions and stale assumptions.
- The stale comments around the issuer adapter and FMS handlers are not behavior bugs today, but they create bad follow-on guidance for future edits because they describe a substrate that no longer exists in production.

## Open questions

None.

+- 2. DI-2026-05-18-001 substrate half is closed in the transfer path. The old flatten/inflate sites are gone from the planet load/unload branches: `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:195-207` pop via `planet.pop_staging_yard_typed()`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:331-348` use typed rollback via `planet.add_to_staging_yard(typed)`, `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:385-388` unload typed `CarriedVehicle` directly, and `game/strategy/engine/order_handlers/transfer_branches.py:407-432` unload typed `DropPod` directly. +- 3. Blocker: `TransferValidator` still rejects real planet staging yards for `drop_pod` loads. In `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:226-231`, `_validate_load()` accepts only `list` and resets any non-list `staging_yard` to `[]`. Real `Planet.staging_yard` is now a `tuple` per `game/strategy/data/planet.py:330-340`, so planet to fleet drop-pod loads validate as empty even when pods are present. I verified this with a read-only runtime probe: a real `Planet` with one staged pod printed `tuple` for `type(planet.staging_yard).__name__` and then returned `False / "P has no items in staging yard."` from `TransferValidator._validate_load(...)`. By contrast, the typed vehicle path is correct: `game/strategy/validation/transfer_validator.py:340-393` iterates the tuple and accepts typed `CarriedVehicle`, and a runtime probe returned `True`.

The UI reader no longer has the list-only silent-skip bug: `game/ui/screens/strategy_detail_fmt.py:284-316` handles `list | tuple` and typed `CarriedVehicle` / `DropPod` with dict fallback. The DTO and facade snapshot paths do the same at `game/strategy/facade/dto/planet_dto.py:115-146` and `game/strategy/facade/slices/planet_slice.py:194-226`.
